openwrt_wiki.Einleitung: The NanoPi R4S is made by FriendlyElec for IoT applications. It includes the RK3399 SoC, two 1Gbps Ethernet ports, microSD storage, and 4GB LPDDR4 RAM. The NanoPi R4S Enterprise Edition adds an additional EEPROM for the MAC address. These models are supported by official builds of OpenWrt. The R4S model with 1GB RAM and the R4SE with onboard 32GB eMMC are not officially supported however have custom builds available.
openwrt_wiki.Installation: Decompress the OpenWrt ...sysupgrade.img.gz image and write it to a micro SD card using software such as dd or Balena Etcher. Then simply insert the SD card into the R4S, apply power, and it will boot OpenWrt.
openwrt_wiki.Hinweis 1GB: The 1GB model is currently not bootable from snapshot. For this model use one of the unofficial builds linked below: anaelorlinski/OpenWrt-NanoPi-R2S-R4S-Builds, immortalwrt/immortalwrt, quintus-lab/OpenWRT-Rockchip
openwrt_wiki.Serial: See photos picture. Serial UART is between USB C port and WAN port.
openwrt_wiki.Warnung Gehaeuse: With console or internal USB2 tail attached, you will have to drill a hole in the side and modify the connectors as the case sits flush to the top of the Ethernet ports!
openwrt_wiki.RTC: RTC backup current is 27uA. Connector P/N: Molex 53398-0271. 1.27/1.25mm RTC battery input connector. A bios battery will NOT fit in the case.
openwrt_wiki.Opening the case: Remove all cables and the SDCard. There are 4 rubber/foam pads covering the screws. Remove them then unscrew all 4 screws. With the base removed, there are a further 2 screws holding the board into the case. Remove them and then tilt the case and tip the board out. It will NOT come out if the SDCard is still inserted.
openwrt_wiki.CPU Management: IRQ-/RPS-Affinitaet fuer eth0/eth1 auf A53/A72-Kerne, Hinweis auf SQM-Optimierungsanleitung
openwrt_wiki.Bootlog OpenWrt: Linux version 5.4.163, Machine model: FriendlyElec NanoPi R4S, Memory: 3959100K/4061184K available

rockchip: add NanoPi R4S support

Hardware
--------
RockChip RK3399 ARM64 (6 cores)
4GB LPDDR4 RAM
2x 1000 Base-T
3 LEDs (LAN / WAN / SYS)
1 Button (Reset)
Micro-SD slot
2x USB 3.0 Port

Installation
------------
Uncompress the OpenWrt sysupgrade and write it to a micro SD card using

openwrt_git_support.01_leds: wan: green:wan an eth0; lan: green:lan an eth1

openwrt_git_support.dts_patch_kernel: rk3399-nanopi-r4s.dts (Kernel v5.13): "Rockchip RK3399 SoC, 1GB DDR3 or 4GB LPDDR4 RAM, Gigabit Ethernet (WAN), Gigabit Ethernet (PCIe) (LAN), USB 3.0 Port x 2, MicroSD slot, Reset button, WAN - LAN - SYS LED"; LEDs green:lan GPIO1_A1, red:sys GPIO0_B5 (default on), green:wan GPIO1_A0; reset GPIO1_C6 KEY_RESTART; pcie0 max-link-speed 1, num-lanes 1
openwrt_git_support.dts_eeprom_patch: NanoPi R4S has a EEPROM attached to the 2nd I2C bus (U92), which stores the MAC address. eeprom@51 microchip,24c02, read-only

openwrt_git_mac.nachricht: rockchip: ensure NanoPi R4S has unique MAC address. FriendlyElec ship two versions of the R4S: The standard as well as the enterprise edition with only the enterprise edition including the EEPROM chip that stores the unique MAC address. In order to assign both board types unique MAC addresses, fall back on the same method used for the NanoPi R2S in case the EEPROM chip is not present by generating the board MAC from the SD card CID.

openwrt_git_uhs.nachricht: rockchip: disable UHS modes for NanoPi R4S. The NanoPi R4S leaves the SD card in 1.8V signalling when rebooting while U-Boot requires the card to be in 3.3V mode. Remove UHS support from the SD controller so the card remains in 3.3V mode. This reduces transfer speeds but ensures a reboot whether from userspace or following a kernel panic is always working.

openwrt_git_enterprise.nachricht: rockchip: add NanoPi R4S Enterprise Edition build. FriendlyElec renamed the NanoPi R4S board with EEPROM (mac address) to "enterprise" edition, and it was added as a "new" board in upstream kernel. This patch switched to use that upstreamed dts and removed local EEPROM patch.

openwrt_git_pcie.nachricht: rockchip: backport pcie fix for rk3399. This patch resolves the LAN port not initializing on the FriendlyElec NanoPI R4S, especially during warm reboots. Upstream: torvalds/linux c3fe7071e196. The NanoPI R4S has its LAN port connected to the RK3399 via PCIE. Since the PCIE lanes don't initialize correctly after reboot, the LAN port doesn't initialize.

friendlyelec_wiki.Introduction: The NanoPi R4S uses the RK3399 SoC. It has two Gbps Ethernet ports and 1G/4G DDR4 RAM. FriendlyElec ported an OpenWrt system for it.
Hardware Spec: CPU: big.LITTLE, Dual-Core Cortex-A72(up to 2.0GHz) + Quad-Core Cortex-A53(up to 1.5GHz)
GPU: Mali-T864 GPU, supports OpenGL ES1.1/2.0/3.0/3.1, OpenCL, DX11, and AFBC
VPU: 4K VP9 and 4K 10bits H265/H264 60fps decoding, Dual VOP, etc
PMU: RK808-D PMIC, cooperated with independent DC/DC, enabling DVFS, software power-down, RTC wake-up, system sleep mode
Ethernet: one Native Gigabit Ethernet, and one PCIe Gigabit Ethernet
Pin header extension interface: 2x5-pin header: SPI x 1, I2C x 1; 4-pin header: USB 2.0
Debug: one Debug UART, 3 Pin 2.54mm header, 3V level, 1500000bps
LEDs: 1 x power LED and 3 x GPIO Controlled LED (SYS, LAN, WAN)
others: 2 Pin 1.27/1.25mm RTC battery input connector; one User Button; one 5V Fan connector
Power supply: DC 5V/3A, via USB-C connector or Pin header
friendlyelec_wiki.USB Port: Each USB 3.0 port has 2A overcurrent protection.
friendlyelec_wiki.RTC: RTC backup current is 27uA. Connector P/N: Molex 53398-0271
friendlyelec_wiki.Notes: Power Input : 5V/3A, via USB Type-C(USB PD Specification is not supported) or Pin1&Pin2 of the 2x5-pin header
friendlyelec_wiki.Differences Standard/Enterprise: The R4S Enterprise version has a built-in EEPROM chip (Model: 24AA025E48T) which has a globally unique MAC address. The R4S Standard version doesn't have this chip and has a MAC address that is generated by a software utility. Apart from this difference, the two versions have the same hardware configuration. Both have the same network chips (RealTek RTL8211E and R8111H). The globally unique MAC address is by default allocated to the CPU's internal Ethernet (rtl8211e), device eth0. This device is named "LAN2" on the PCB and "WAN" on the board's case. How to check: If bit 2 of the first byte is 1, the address is only used locally, not globally unique.
friendlyelec_wiki.Essentials You Need: MicroSD Card/TF Card: Class 10 or Above, minimum 8GB SDHC; 5V/3A and above USB Type-C interface power adapter (Note: QC/PD fast charger may have compatibility issues), empfohlen 5V 4A Power Adapter
friendlyelec_wiki.Known Issues: Q: UGREEN 18W QC power adapter cannot power R4S? A: It needs to wait for a few seconds to work normally.

friendlyelec_shop.Hinweis: Due to the shortage of the chip that has a unique built-in MAC address, we no longer list the R4S board with a unique MAC address for retail sales. If you want to order the R4S board with a unique MAC address, you have to place an order with a minimum order quantity of 100 pieces.
